Subject: Medilink - MSA redlines & SCCs appendix proposal

Hi Rachel,

Thanks for the demo last week. Attached are Medilink's redlines to the MSA + Order Form. There are three items that are blocking procurement right now and we wanted to surface them early so we can avoid a long back-and-forth:

1) SCCs appendix: procurement requires an explicit "SCCs Appendix" with the new EU Standard Contractual Clauses referenced and an exhibit that maps processing activities to SCC clauses. We included a draft appendix in the attached redline.

2) Audit clause / cost responsibility: we need clarity that customer audit rights are limited to remote evidence requests and that audit costs for third-party assessments will be paid by the processor only if noncompliance is found. Medilink's standard language shifts all third-party audit costs to the vendor; we are prepared to negotiate a middle ground (cost-share or cap).

3) Subprocessor notice period: procurement currently requires 90 days' advance notice for new subprocessors. Please confirm if Redwood can accept 90 days or propose an alternative.

Attachments: Medilink_MSA_redlines.docx (docx, ~98KB)

Can you please loop in your legal/ops and let us know which items Redwood can agree to and which need pilot exceptions? We are hoping to finalize contractual terms this month.

Best,

Anya Petrova

Rachel / Anya —

Thanks for the ping. I reviewed Medilink's redlines and put together a focused response and suggested DPA language. High-level: we can accommodate an SCCs appendix and tighter notice/controls for subprocessors, but we need hard carveouts around audit scope and commercial liability.

Key proposed points (draft language below):

1) SCCs Appendix: Add "Appendix B (Standard Contractual Clauses)" referencing the 2021 EU SCCs, with a table mapping Processing Activity -> Purpose -> Applicable SCC Clause. We will provide the table; Medilink should confirm any additions related to special category data.

2) Audit rights and costs: Propose the following clause to replace Medilink's broader ask:

"Vendor shall permit Customer to conduct remote assessments (including requests for logs and system configurations) to verify Vendor's compliance with the DPA. On-site audits shall be permitted only where Customer provides specific, documented evidence of material non-compliance and shall be subject to Vendor's reasonable security and operational constraints. If an audit (remote or on-site) identifies material non-compliance attributable to Vendor, Vendor shall reimburse Customer for reasonable third-party audit costs up to a cap of EUR 12,000 per audit engagement. If no material non-compliance is identified, Customer shall bear the cost of the audit."
3) Subprocessor notice: Vendor will provide 30 days' advance notice for new subprocessors and an expedited review process (7 business days) for critical/regulated subprocessors with an option to request additional documentation. If Medilink requires a longer notice period for specific categories, please identify them and we will consider a targeted 45-day notice for those classes.

I attached a redline DPA with the snippet above included (rki_proposed_DPA_redline.docx).

Questions for Medilink:
- Do you require on-site audits as a matter of policy or only in escalations?
- Are there particular subprocessors you expect to be high risk that would justify a longer notice period?

If we can agree on the audit-cost cap and remote-first audits, I think we can keep the rest to appendix-level negotiation and close quickly.

Best,
Ben Carter
Senior Counsel | Redwood Inference

Rachel / Ben —

Appreciate the quick turnaround and proposed language. A few points from procurement/legal after an internal check:

- Remote-first audits are acceptable. We will only request on-site audits where remote evidence is insufficient to establish compliance. That said, our audit playbook expects vendor cooperation with on-site visits if there is a material breach. We can accept the proposed EUR 12,000 cap if Redwood confirms it applies per audit engagement rather than per year.

- Subprocessor notice: Medilink can move to 45 days for newly added subprocessors (compromise from 90). For core platform subprocessors (hosting, KMS), procurement will ask for 60 days and a short onboarding questionnaire. Can Redwood confirm whether core subprocessors are on a different cadence?

- SCCs Appendix: procurement will review the mapping table and provide any special-category flags by Friday.

We can sign off on a mutual action plan if Redwood legal confirms the 45/60-day split for subprocessors and the EUR 12,000 per-audit cap (per Ben's wording).
